title: The Giant Easter Egg
seo_title: Easter Egg Charcuterie Board: Spring Showpiece & What to Buy
description: A giant Easter egg charcuterie board for 12 to 15: an egg outlined in pretzels and painted in stripes of ham, cheddar, Havarti, mozzarella and spring vegetables.
hook: One enormous decorated egg, painted in food.
why: The egg is a pretzel fence: a long oval of pretzels holds everything in place, so the stripes stay neat. Rolled ham, mortadella ruffles, cheddar, Havarti zigzags and mozzarella pearls make the bands of color.
Yellow peppers and spring vegetables add the pastel tones. It's built for Easter brunch and spring family gatherings, and kids love it.

timeline.what: Cube the cheeses and melons, slice the cucumber, cut the Havarti triangles, and roll the ham. Store everything separately, covered.
Lay the pretzel-stick egg outline and the stripe dividers.
Fill the stripes from top to bottom, then build the outside.

faq.q: How do you make an Easter egg charcuterie board?
faq.a: Outline a large egg in pretzels, then fill it in horizontal stripes of ham, cheese and vegetables, like a painted egg.
Yes. It's mild ham, cheddar, Havarti and vegetables.

Cut the cheese and vegetables the day before. Keep meat, cheese and cut fruit out no more than 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F. For a long party, build half, keep the refill in the fridge and top it up halfway through.
